problem: Semantic-only open-vocabulary detection (e.g. OVIR-3D) cannot disambiguate among multiple instances of the same category, while existing 3D scene graphs use closed-set labels and predefined relations, so they cannot take free-form context-aware queries.
motivation: Humans specify entities using context ("the cup on the kitchen table", "Mary's favorite cup"), and robots need to ground such references for navigation and manipulation. Scene graphs capture context, but only if categories and relations are predefined, so replacing discrete labels with open-vocabulary features is needed.
key_idea: Build an open-vocabulary 3D scene graph whose nodes and edges carry language-aligned features, parse the free-form query into a star-shaped query graph with an LLM, and ground the target by sub-graph matching with candidate proposal and likelihood re-ranking.
insight: Adding relational context to open-vocabulary detection raises Top-1 grounding success (e.g. 35.2 to 51.1 on DOVE-G BB with OVSG-L vs OVIR-3D), while Top-3 gains are small because OVIR-3D already retrieves the right category. The likelihood similarity (OVSG-L) beats Jaccard and Szymkiewicz-Simpson, which depend on hard thresholds (Jaccard is often worse than OVIR-3D). Performance drops when relation vocabulary is varied freely, showing the spatial-language encoder is a bottleneck.
method: OVSG representation: nodes (object/agent/region) hold type, open-vocab feature, optional text and 3D box; edges hold spatial or abstract relations with features; distance is 1-dot product, or a learned SRP for spatial relations
Scene graph construction: OVIR-3D fuses RGBD into instances with Detic features; agent/region names, positions and abstract relations come from user input
Query parsing: an LLM (GPT-3.5/LLaMA) with ~10 chain-of-thought few-shot examples converts the query into a target plus entities and typed relations, forming a star-graph G_q

Type-specific encoders: CLIP-text for query objects (aligned with Detic), Sentence-BERT for agents/regions, GloVe for abstract relations (sentiment-sensitive), and a trained spatial pose encoder + CLIP-text predictor for spatial relations
Sub-graph matching: rank all scene nodes by distance to the query center node, extract local subgraphs as candidates, and re-rank by graph similarity
Graph similarity variants: Likelihood (OVSG-L, product of max node×edge likelihoods, σv=1, σe=2), Jaccard (OVSG-J) and Szymkiewicz-Simpson (OVSG-S) with thresholded matches
Spatial relationship predictor: 5-layer MLP over pose pairs (18-d) plus CLIP text feature, trained with BCE on synthetic data (8 base relations, 90 descriptions)

setting.backbone: OVIR-3D (Detic features) + GPT-3.5/LLaMA query parser (frozen) + CLIP/Sentence-BERT/GloVe encoders + small trained spatial MLP predictor
setting.training_data: Only the spatial relationship encoder/predictor is trained, on synthetic data (8 basic spatial relations, 90 descriptions); the rest is pretrained/frozen
setting.observation: RGBD scan of the whole scene with poses, plus user-provided agent/region names, positions and abstract relations
setting.action_space: None for grounding (outputs a 3D box of the entity); robots navigate with a ROS nav stack (TEB planner) to the grounded position, and manipulate by moving the gripper to the box center
setting.simulator: None (offline scene datasets ScanNet, ICL-NUIM, DOVE-G; real robots)
setting.privileged: Agent/region positions and abstract relations are given as user input; ScanNet and ICL-NUIM/DOVE-G ground-truth annotations are used to build evaluation queries; scenes are fully pre-scanned

numbers_note: Custom grounding benchmarks (not standard navigation benchmarks); GSR = Grounding Success Rate. Real-robot results reported in appendix tables (nav: 6/7 objects 100%; manipulation OVSG 0.88/0.75/0.75 vs OVIR-3D 0/0.75/0.33 over 3 scenes). Some details in figures only.
results: OVSG-L beats OVIR-3D on all three datasets, e.g. Top-1 BB grounding success 58.85 vs 38.56 (ScanNet Whole), 54.25 vs 35.5 (DOVE-G Whole), and 74.09 vs 39.28 (ICL-NUIM Whole). It also far exceeds ConceptFusion on ICL-NUIM (3D success 2.64-7.37 average).
limitations: Depends on the quality of the open-vocabulary fusion (OVIR-3D); missed or mis-segmented instances cannot be grounded
Depends on an LLM to parse queries; parse errors give wrong outputs and performance drops with varied relation wording
Likelihood multiplication may not balance node and edge types well; GNN attempts failed; star-graph assumption; agent/region positions assumed given
